text: You arrive already past the introduction. Your Pluto sits on their Sun, and their Sun is where they ask to be recognized and taken at their word. You cannot take them at their word. This is not suspicion. You read the reason under the stated reason, without effort and often without deciding to, and they can tell it is happening. For them the experience is never neutral. Being looked at that closely can be the first time anyone bothered, and it can also feel like a door opened without a knock. Around you their presentation stops working, so they either get more definite, saying plainly what they want, or they hold the surface harder. Many people do both in the same month. The effect on their vitality is concentration. Things they had been carrying loosely acquire weight: the plan they mention and never begin, the account of their life they give at parties. You are not lecturing anyone. Your function works by pressure rather than by argument, and here the pressure falls on identity itself. People close to this contact tend to make decisions they had put off for years, and they are not always grateful at the time. What comes back gets written about less and matters as much. Their Sun falls on your buried material. You are used to being the one who sees; in their company you are lit. What you handle privately becomes visible without anyone digging, because daylight has no need to dig. After years of carrying your own depth alone that can be an unfamiliar ease. It can also feel like standing in a doorway with the hall light on behind you. A conjunction offers no vantage point. You cannot watch this from outside, so your investment in who they turn out to be can outgrow whatever the connection actually is. You may catch yourself caring about their choices with a force that surprises you. That force is the aspect. Nothing in a chart describes conduct, and this one predicts nothing about what either of you will do with what you see. One asymmetry deserves naming. Your reading of them is usually accurate and always partial. You see the machinery. You do not see what it is like to be them running it. Treated as authority, accuracy narrows the connection into a single story about who they are, told by you. Kept as information, it becomes one of the rarer things one person can give another: being met at full depth by someone who did not look away. The long form of this is that you learn the difference between seeing someone and deciding for them. That distinction does not come naturally to a person built the way you are, and this contact will keep teaching it until it takes.

What you have here is a door that opens from your side and never swings on its own. Your Pluto stands at an easy remove from their Sun. Your depth is within reach of their identity, and nothing in the geometry makes either of you use it. Weeks go by in ordinary company. Then one conversation goes somewhere, and the difference afterward is obvious to both of you. Used, your effect on them is clarifying. They describe a plan, or a version of themselves, and you ask the one question that goes underneath it. You are not confronting anyone. Your timing is good at this angle, which is most of what a sextile is, so the blunt sentence arrives at the moment they can take it. They leave more decided than they came, and they tend to return the next time something needs facing rather than discussing. Their half of the trade is that they give your intensity a legitimate use. Depth with no application turns inward and gets heavy. Pointed at a person with a clear direction and a working sense of self, it becomes practical. You can see where the leverage sits in what they are attempting, and saying so costs you nothing and helps them considerably. Being useful with the part of yourself that most rooms have no use for is not a small thing to be handed. There is warmth in it for you as well. Their vitality does not shrink from your seriousness and does not need managing around it. You get to be at full strength without watching for the moment somebody gets uncomfortable. For a person whose depth has been called too much elsewhere, that alone can change how you carry it. Silence is how this one fails, not friction. Nothing insists. You can know them for a decade, feel certain the two of you could go anywhere, and never once go, because the lighter conversation is always on hand and nothing forces the other. Left alone, the contact settles into a vague sense that they are interesting and you are close, with no evidence behind either impression. In shared work it shows up on anything requiring nerve. They hold the direction and take the visible position. You can see what the situation actually costs and which people are carrying that cost. That pairing does well wherever the polite account of a situation is not the accurate one. Among friends or relatives it looks like the person who gets the true version from you and gives one back. Every deliberate use widens the channel a little. Over years it adds up to someone who has seen you at your least diplomatic and stayed, which is the entire return on an angle that never once demanded anything.

Their confidence is the exact thing you cannot take at face value. Your Pluto squares their Sun, so when they are brightest and most certain about who they are, something in you goes to work on it. You notice what the certainty is covering. You notice the ambition sitting under the modest description. Often you say nothing at all, and the nothing is loud. From their chair, you are pressure applied to the place where they most want acknowledgment. Other people give them the ordinary nod. You give them a pause. They state a preference and receive a question about the motive behind it. They present a version of themselves and feel it being weighed. A square does not blend two functions, it makes each one obstruct the other, and what gets obstructed here is a straightforward wish to be seen. You contribute to this without choosing to. Your depth does not arrive as an opinion that can be argued with. It arrives as weight, and weight lands whether or not you aimed it. This is worth knowing precisely because you may experience yourself as merely observing while they experience being pressed. Both accounts are honest. Neither is the whole picture. What comes back at you is a refusal to be reduced. Their Sun keeps asserting a self you have decided is only part of the story, and it keeps not going away. That is a genuine check on you. You are used to holding the deepest read in the room, and here is a person whose plain insistence on their own account survives your attention. You cannot dig them into agreement. The friction carries traction. Nothing they inherited, borrowed, or kept because it was easy to keep will get past you unexamined, and what survives that becomes theirs in a way it was not before. In return, their directness keeps calling your suspicion into the open where it can be tested. You find out which of your readings are perception and which are only habit. Squares run in cycles. Pressure gathers, something finally gets said, the air clears for a while, and it begins again around a slightly different subject. In shared work the result can be unusually rigorous, since neither of you can float a weak idea past the other, though comfort is not on the menu. Among friends or family it tends to organize around who gets to describe the other person accurately. The workable version is not the friction ending. It is you offering the reading as one view rather than the verdict, and letting their insistence stand without needing to see through it. Do that often enough and your depth stops being something they have to survive and turns into something they can use.

Your intensity has somewhere to go with them, which is not the usual arrangement. A trine between your Pluto and their Sun means the serious end of you meets their sense of self without setting off any alarms. They do not find you heavy. They find you steady, and that difference in reception is the aspect. What you do for them is back their existence with more force than shows on the surface. You invest in what they are building. You speak for them in rooms they are not in. When their confidence goes down you stay where you are, because a shaken person does not frighten you and you have no need for them to be fine. People with that behind them tend to attempt things in public they would not attempt alone, and they often cannot say where the nerve came from. You also see them accurately without it landing as an accusation. You can tell when the stated reason is not the reason, and here you can say so and be heard, since your accuracy arrives attached to obvious commitment rather than to a case being built. That combination is rare enough that they may bring you material they hand to nobody else. The return is that their clarity gives your depth a direction. Left to itself, intensity like yours circles. It finds the buried thing, then finds it again. Their Sun has an aim, and an aim is exactly what your function lacks. Pointed at something with a shape, your depth becomes work that produces results instead of pressure with nowhere to land. Ease is the risk. A trine hands over the capacity and withholds the reason to spend it. You can hold this contact for a decade, feel the depth sitting there, and spend the whole time on ordinary conversation, because nothing in the geometry will interrupt you. Available and unused looks identical to available. The subtler problem is influence nobody examines. Your read on them is usually right, so they begin checking with you about who they are. That is flattering and it accumulates quietly. A picture of a person, however generous and however accurate, is still a picture, and someone who defers to yours has stopped drawing their own. You will not notice this happening. Neither will they. Kept in use, this becomes durable in a way most connections are not. You know what they are made of underneath the presentation, and they know that you know, so a bad stretch does not require rebuilding the introduction. The work is deliberate. Take them the thing that unsettles you instead of saving your depth for their crises, and hand back some of the authority you have been given.

You stand opposite the part of them that faces outward. Their Sun does the presenting: the identity, the wish to be recognized, the account of themselves given in daylight. You are at the other end, holding everything that account leaves out. Neither position can see itself, and each of you happens to be standing exactly where the other has no view. Their presentation gets no purchase on you. You do not attack it. You simply decline to treat it as the whole matter, and they can feel their certainty being measured rather than received. Around you they may perform their identity harder, insisting on a version of themselves with more force than the moment calls for, because your attention makes it feel unproven. Or they open the whole thing and tell you what they have never told anyone. Oppositions produce both, often from the same person in the same year. What you encounter in them is a ceiling on depth. They keep asserting a self that is simple, visible, and not going anywhere, and your instinct to find the thing underneath keeps meeting a person who is, in a real sense, what they appear to be. That is infuriating. It is also useful, since nobody else in your life stands still under your reading and comes through intact. The charge in this runs high and deserves plain description. Each of you registers as a fact the other has to account for. Oppositions seldom fade out quietly; they either work or they keep restarting. A contest tends to form over who gets to say what is really going on, and each of you will be sure you are the reasonable party. All of that belongs to the angle. It is not evidence about anybody, and it forecasts nothing about how either person behaves. The trap is assignment. You can end up carrying the entire depth of the connection, cast as the difficult one while they hold the sensible position, and it is a role you may accept without argument because it is familiar. They can hand you all of it just as easily. Each of you is holding one end of something shared, and the end in your hand is not the object. An opposition is not only a standoff. The two ends complete each other, and that is available here. Your reading of them is seldom mistaken and never the whole account. What they bring you is a directness you do not generate on your own, and a self that does not dissolve under scrutiny. When neither of you needs to win the point, they get something few people ever get: a description of themselves that includes the parts they cannot see. You get proof that depth can be met by daylight without either one going out.

You get in under the guard before either of you has decided anything. Their Moon is the reflex layer: what settles them, what they reach for at the end of a bad day, the mood they hold as a baseline. Your Pluto sits directly on it. From your side the strange part is how quickly the ordinary disappears. Small talk with them will not hold. You are three layers down by the second cup of tea and neither of you steered there. What your depth does to their comfort is refuse the smooth version of it. Their habits work partly by keeping certain things quiet, and the quiet does not hold as well in your company. Feelings they had filed as settled come back up with the original weight still on them. Sometimes you ask. More often you are simply present, and presence is enough, since your function does not need a question to reach something. For them this cuts both ways and usually both at once. They are not being asked to perform an easier mood than the one they have, which is a relief most people never get offered. They are also being seen at a depth nobody scheduled, in the part of themselves that was never meant for an audience. Some move toward that and some pull back, and the same person often does both. Their Moon gives you something you are short of. Your intensity has no ordinary outlet and does not know what to do with a Tuesday. Their instinct for comfort supplies one: the shape of an evening, food at a normal hour, the small repetitions that make a week. Heavy material becomes livable once it is attached to somebody's routine, and you may find yourself leaning on that floor harder than you expected. The charge in a conjunction gathers around feeling and who is holding it. You may track their mood more closely than you track almost anything, and know before they do that something has shifted. They may find their needs pulling at a place in you that is usually shut. That accuracy is the aspect working. What either of you does with it is not written anywhere in a chart. What tends to change is the definition of safe between you. The thin version of comfort will not survive this contact. What replaces it is built from material that has already been looked at rather than material kept out of sight, and it holds better under load for exactly that reason. Your own share of the change is quieter. Being close to reflexes that legible teaches you the cost of accuracy, and the difference between knowing what someone feels and being welcome in it. That distinction is not a natural one for you. Here it stops being avoidable.

Their feelings are within reach of your depth, and reach is all it is. A sextile between your Pluto and their Moon gives you access to the part of them that runs on instinct, with no obligation attached in either direction. Whole seasons pass in pleasant company. Then one evening something true gets said, and the connection is not the same afterward. When you do go there, the effect on them is permission. They can bring you the actual trouble rather than the tidied one, because their heaviest feelings do not alarm you and do not have to be made presentable first. That is uncommon. Most people need a mood softened before they can receive it, and everyone knows which of their friends those are. You are not one of them, and they find that out early. You are also useful at the point of noticing. You register a shift in them before they have named it, and at this angle you can say so without it arriving as intrusion. The timing is the gift. What would be excavation from a harder contact reads here as somebody paying attention. Their Moon does something for you that is harder to see. Your intensity has no small setting. It runs on pressure and does not scale down to a Wednesday on its own. Their instinct for comfort shows you the lower register: the short message, the ordinary kindness, the gesture that costs nothing and steadies a person anyway. You can learn to offer that, and it tends to surprise anyone who has only met your other end. The limitation is structural. Nothing here compels. Two people can carry this angle for fifteen years and use it three times, and the company stays good throughout, which is precisely why neither of them goes looking. An unopened door makes no noise. You will not miss what you never noticed was there. In a difficult stretch this is a real resource and not a rescue. You can usually get through to them, and they can usually take what you bring, but one of you has to start, and in a bad week neither of you will. Used on purpose, it stops being an occasion and becomes ordinary. You raise the heavy subject early instead of once it has set. They hand over the part they normally carry by themselves. Every use makes the next one easier, and a few years of that produces something most pairs never build, with no crisis in its history to explain where it came from.

You want the real thing; they want the day to settle. That is the collision in full. Your Pluto squares their Moon, so your instinct to go under a surface keeps arriving exactly when they have finally got the surface calm. A square does not blend two functions. It makes each interrupt the other, and the interruption is where anything happens. From where you sit, their comfort can look like avoidance. They calm it down, change the subject, give it a few days, and to you that reads as a decision not to look. From where they sit, your persistence lands as force. Neither reading is malicious. Both are sincere, which is why the disagreement never resolves at the level it gets held. What your depth does to their reflexes is take away the easy setting. Moods they would have absorbed alone become visible, because they meet something that will not treat them as small. Attachments they keep unexamined get tested. That is genuinely hard on the part of a person built to run on pattern, and the difficulty is not a weakness in them. A Moon is supposed to work by habit. Yours is the function that makes habit impossible. Their side presses on you harder than most things do. Their needs are daily, plain, and repetitive, and depth is poor at daily, plain, and repetitive. They want responsiveness on a normal evening. You can carry enormous weight and still be caught out by that request, and it is one of the few pressures that makes a function like yours negotiate instead of dig in. The consumer version of this aspect calls it harm, and that is a category error. What the angle fixes is that two functions will press on each other. Who presses, how, and what either of you does about it are not in the chart. A pair holding this square can build something that gets taken apart and rebuilt more than once, or a long stalemate where one guards and one pursues, and nothing in the geometry chooses between them. The compensation is traction, and there is a great deal of it. Nothing between you gets to coast, and that is worth more than it feels like at the time. Over time they lose the ability to hold a false calm in front of you, which is uncomfortable and also worth having. You lose the ability to believe that intensity by itself counts as care. The growth is in learning what your weight costs when it lands on somebody's ordinary week. Each time you bring your depth without insisting the room match it, and each time they meet you without smoothing it away, both of you discover the footing is steadier than the reflex assumed. None of that arrives once and stays fixed. The angle keeps putting the question, and a question is not a verdict.

Heavy material travels well between you. Your Pluto reaches their Moon without meeting resistance, so the serious end of you connects to the instinctive part of them and neither has to build anything for it to work. The ease is the aspect, and it is worth examining precisely because it costs nothing. The part of themselves that most company edges away from is the part you are steady around. Whatever they carry that does not get said lightly can be said to you at a normal volume. You do not treat it as a spectacle and you do not need it softened first. Other people find your quality heavy. They find it steady. Neither of you arranged that difference. You also read their moods accurately with no effort, and at this angle the accuracy does not feel to them like surveillance. You know when a mood is about the thing they said it was about and when it is not. You can say so, and they rarely bother arguing. That spares the two of you an entire category of misunderstanding. Their Moon gives your intensity a place to set down. Few people can offer that and stay comfortable in the room. Depth like yours generally has to be held somewhere, managed, kept at a level other people can tolerate, and here is a person around whom you can put it down. Effort you did not know you were making simply stops. The thing to watch here is drift. Nothing about an easy contact ever asks to be used. Because the exchange runs on its own, it can run on habit: the two of you treating depth as a routine and mistaking a well-worn path for new ground. Nothing in this contact will interrupt the groove for you. There is a quieter risk in how much traffic ends up here. If you turn into the only place their feelings get to be true, and they turn into the only place yours get set down, both of you quietly stop practicing anywhere else, and no one ever decides that should happen. What accumulates, when it gets used rather than coasted on, is durability. You know what they are made of at the level where people are actually made, and a bad stretch does not require establishing that again. It is already established. Whether this bond stays close or moves to the background of your life, the knowledge stays with both of you, and it changes what each of you expects a person to be able to hold.

Across from you sits a person who needs the day to be manageable. Your Pluto faces their Moon, and nothing in that arrangement blends. You hold what is real and unfinished. They hold what is familiar and survivable. Each of you is looking straight at something you do not carry yourself. In your company, their comforts keep getting looked at. Their Moon runs on repetition: known reassurances, a short list of people, a Sunday that looks like last Sunday. You go to the place where the repetition wears thin and you stay there, often without meaning to and sometimes without saying a word. Being opposite that is uncomfortable. It is also clarifying, because they find out quickly which of their comforts carry weight and which are merely old. What comes back is harder for you to dismiss than you might expect. Their need is ordinary and it is constant. They want warmth on a normal evening, delivered plainly, more than once. That request does not go away across an opposition, and it reaches you where an argument could not. You can be entirely capable of holding somebody's worst material and still be caught out by being asked for something small and regular. The pull runs strong in both directions. Attachment here can outrun what you would have predicted for yourself, and neutrality about them may simply not be on offer. They may find the same. The charge is a property of the angle. It is not evidence about anybody, and it does not predict a single thing either of you will do. There is a particular trap in an opposition, which is that each of you swells into an exaggerated version of your own half. You get more relentless because they appear to be dodging. They get more protective because you appear to be pressing. Neither of those people is actually in the room. Both are manufactured by the angle. Oppositions do not only pull; they also fill in. On its own your depth curdles, since nothing ever lightens what it keeps turning up. On its own their comfort goes brittle, since nothing tests it. In contact the two correct each other, and the correction happens whenever you let their need for solid ground count as a real claim rather than an evasion, and they let your reading of a situation change what they were ready to believe about it. What years of this tend to leave you with is range. You learn that intensity is not the only serious thing in a room, and that the ability to make a bad day survivable is a skill rather than a failure of nerve. Your own chart was never going to teach you that. It arrives from across the table or not at all.

Their sentences land in you somewhere deeper than they were aimed. Your Pluto sits on their Mercury, and the whole business of sorting, asking, and talking now happens under your weight. Something they said in passing is still with you a year later. A question asked to fill a pause gets taken seriously enough to change something. They learn this early, and it changes how they talk. What your depth does to their speech is remove the shallow end. They cannot be idle with you. Every sentence gets weighed, and someone who feels their sentences being weighed becomes either far more careful or far more honest. Plenty of people become both, in different rooms. Some describe it as the first time anybody actually listened. Others find they have lost the ability to chat, and that is a genuine loss, not a small one. You also hear what they are not saying. Their word choices give them away to you: the subject they route around, the story that arrives in the same shape every time. You may know what a silence of theirs contains, which is unsettling to be on the receiving end of even when nobody mentions it. What comes back is the thing your function most lacks. You carry material that has never been in words. Their Mercury finds language for it, sometimes carelessly and sometimes exactly, and naming changes what is named. A pressure you have held shapelessly acquires edges and a size. Neither of you is likely to call that a service, and it is one. It also explains why an offhand phrase from them can hit you far harder than they meant it to. The strain in a conjunction is that there is no gap. Silence between you is never empty. A subject they walk past registers as a decision. A pause of yours gets read for hours. The two of you can lose a week to interpretation that one direct question would have ended. You assume they missed it; they assume the same. Both of you are wrong. There is also the pull toward research. Wanting to know how a mind like theirs got assembled is not a passing interest for you, and it does not run out by itself. Where that goes is not decided by the aspect, which describes a charge between two functions and nothing about anyone's behavior. What builds over years is a conversation with no small talk left in it and no pretense either. They stop bothering with the version of an answer that would satisfy somebody else, since it has never once worked on you. That is uncomfortable to arrive at and unusual to have.

You can make a subject sayable for them, whenever either of you decides to. This sextile puts your Pluto within working distance of their Mercury: your tolerance for what is difficult sits beside their machinery for putting things in order. Neither obliges the other. Most conversations stay ordinary, and nothing is lost by that. Where it earns its keep is on the subject they have been talking around for months. You do not flinch when they finally approach it, so the approach goes better than they expected. They get to say the thing in a normal voice, to somebody who will not be alarmed, will not rush to reassure, and will not try to fix it on the spot. People remember conversations like that for years and usually cannot explain what was different. Your effect on their thinking is a steady pull toward what actually matters in a question. They bring you the tidy account of a problem and you decline it once, mildly, and they revise. You are not confrontational at this angle. You are simply unpersuaded by a surface, and the doubt is gentle enough to be usable instead of something they have to defend against. What comes back is order. Your material tends to sit in your chest without a shape. Their Mercury takes it apart into pieces that can be handled one at a time, and a problem split into parts stops being an atmosphere and starts being a list. For a function that otherwise just accumulates, that is a real relief. The two of you are good at finding things out. Give this pairing a document, a family question, a situation with an answer buried somewhere in it, and you will reach the bottom of it. They supply patience and method. You supply the flat unwillingness to take the first answer as the answer. The combination works whether or not either of you is trying. Nothing compels here, which is the standing weakness of the angle. You can talk for years, well and warmly, and never once put the loaded question on the table. Nothing goes wrong. The connection is just smaller than it might have been, and neither of you notices, because a road not taken leaves no evidence behind. Spent on purpose, it changes what the two of you are for each other. They learn that a hard subject can be raised without a scene attached. You learn that your depth is easier to carry once somebody has put words on part of it. Neither of those turns up on its own.

Interrogation is not what you intend. It happens anyway. Your Pluto squares their Mercury, so their ordinary way of naming and sorting a situation keeps running into the part of you that treats information as consequential. They ask a plain question. You hear a position being taken, and you answer the position. From their chair this is tiring in a specific way. They wanted a fact. What arrived was a look, or a pause, or a reply aimed at a motive they did not know they had. They try again with more precision, and the precision reads as evasion. Two or three rounds in, they are explaining why they asked at all, which was, from where they stand, curiosity and nothing else. Some of the time your reading is correct, which is what makes it hard to dismiss and harder to live beside. Your half of the friction is that their plainness lands on material that was not ready to be in the room. Their Mercury puts words on things; that is the whole of its job. You hold the part that is not meant to be spoken yet. A neutral sentence from them can pull it into the open before you had decided anything, and what they intended as description arrives at your end as exposure. So the two of you develop a list of unraised subjects, and nobody drafts it. A topic produces a silence once, then twice, and after that you both route around it automatically. Most of what this aspect does happens in that routing, not in anything either of you says out loud. When it does become an argument, you are not using the same tool. They move fast, stack reasons, and press for a clean statement. You go quiet, or you set down one sentence that moves the discussion onto ground they never meant to defend. Speed does not beat weight and weight does not beat speed. These arguments usually end by being abandoned, and both of you know abandonment is not agreement. Each of you sands down a habit the other could not reach alone. You are the reason they cannot treat a question as neutral, and questions are rarely as neutral as the person asking believes. They are the reason you cannot leave a thing unnamed indefinitely, and a mind that insists on plain sentences is a genuine check on a function that prefers the unspoken. Neither of you would have chosen that service. It gets delivered regardless. What comes of staying in it is that your silence stops being a tactic and becomes a choice you can account for. You will still know things about them they have not said. The change is that you can say why you are not saying it, which is the only form of depth another person can work with.

They can say the buried thing to you in an ordinary voice. Your Pluto trines their Mercury, so the part of you that goes under a situation and the part of them that describes it work with each other instead of across. What costs other pairs years of accumulated trust costs the two of you an afternoon, and neither notices anything unusual about it until you try the same thing with somebody else. Your effect on their thinking is gravity. Left alone, a Mercury stays busy: sorting, comparing, producing accurate accounts of matters that needed no accounting. Your attention keeps landing on the part that actually decides the question, and over time they start going there first. Over time they stop chasing the interesting question and go after the one that decides things. Some will say that talking with you rearranged how they think, and mean it literally. You also make hard subjects speakable rather than dramatic. You receive what they bring as information, not as a disclosure, and that flat reception is what makes handing it over possible at all. Most people carrying something they cannot say have exactly one person for it. With this angle running, you are a strong candidate. What comes back is language. Your function does not produce sentences, it produces weight. Their Mercury turns weight into something with a shape, and does it lightly, with no ceremony attached. Twenty minutes of their talk can do more for a thing you have carried ten years than the ten years did. The failure of an easy angle is overuse. Because depth costs nothing here, everything gets taken there, including matters that were fine where they were. A slow month can get promoted to a mystery, and the two of you will call the promotion intimacy. Plenty of situations are exactly what they look like, and this pair is the last to believe it. There is a second soft spot, and it is shared certainty. You suspect, they articulate, and the articulation makes the suspicion sound settled. A theory about someone else's motives can harden into a fact between you in a single conversation, and nothing in the exchange will ever test it. Once it has hardened, neither of you is standing anywhere that would show the crack. The way this stays worth something is to point it at questions that have answers. Choose one you have both been avoiding, and settle it. The pair of you can reach the bottom of almost anything, and the only waste is reaching the bottom of something that was never going to matter.

They explain, and you listen to everything except the explanation. Your Pluto sits opposite their Mercury, which puts the part of you that knows a stated reason is rarely the working one directly across from a mind whose whole job is stating reasons. Nothing either of you brought to the table will close that gap. Conversations take a shape you come to recognize. They give an account, thorough and reasonable. You do not accept it, sometimes out loud and more often just by declining to be moved, and they can feel the account being measured rather than received. So they add detail. Detail reads as effort, effort reads as something being managed, and you look harder. By midnight neither of you has given an inch and both of you are still talking. What they run into in you is a ceiling on what description can do. They can be exactly right and still hear that they have only accounted for the outside of it. For a mind that works by accounting, that is intolerable, and it is also the only correction that mind is ever likely to receive. Nobody else will offer it, and nobody will offer it gently. Coming back the other way, their talk gives you nowhere to hide. Silence is not an answer they accept. Material you keep underground gets pulled into sentences, sometimes because they asked and sometimes because they named it in passing without noticing what they had touched. That is not always welcome. For a function like yours it is also the only route by which any of it ever gets out. There is a loop here and it closes quickly. The more reasonable they become, the more the reasonableness looks to you like cover, which produces more doubt, which produces more reasoning. Both of you get flattened into caricature, one all daylight and the other all suspicion, and neither caricature is who walked in. It improves when you say the suspicion out loud, in words, at the time you have it. Your instinct is to wait, watch, and let the evidence accumulate until it speaks for itself.
